summary: @servicetitan/marketing-route preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package declares itself as a React marketing-route library but its package.json preinstall hook runs setup.mjs, which downloads the Bun runtime (v1.3.13) from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts and chmod +x's it, and invokes it via execFileSync to run the sibling file math_init.js. math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated bun-cjs bundle (shuffled string/numeric dictionary with an array-shift decoder), and setup.mjs itself uses systematic _0xNNNN identifier renaming and per-function string-array dictionaries to hide its constants. Executing the payload under a freshly-downloaded alternate runtime causes standard Node-based scanners to miss the code that actually runs. The React-route purpose advertised in the package name has no need for a second runtime or an opaque 727KB blob, and the shipped payload is not referenced by any README, exports, or source file. On npm install, attacker-chosen code from math_init.js runs on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
